FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: A2/A3 check of held sources first: the track registry and ND.memo rules.fees say 'none identified.' and rules.feeWaiver 'not applicable; no fee is identified.'; the committed manifest's pay_fee entry says 'none identified.' and its apply_fee_waiver entry is conditional on inability to pay; the route census names no compiled-profile requiredSourceId for this route, and the compiled ND profile's only fee lines ('no filing fee may be charged', 'there is no filing fee') are keyed to the N.D.C.C. 12-60.1 petition to close nonconviction records, a different filing, so under A3 they do not establish this route's answer; the held 13-page official instructions (8ac6b578, packet pages 1-13) say only, on p13, 'If you're required to pay a filing fee and can't afford to pay, complete the Fee Waiver Forms available at ndcourts.gov/legal-self-help/fee-waiver.' So no held source establishes an amount or a no-fee rule and limb 3 of DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 applies. The packet says so on page 32: 'No fee amount is asserted; if a filing fee is required and unaffordable, the original instructions direct concurrent fee-waiver forms. Confirm that conditional input before filing', in the same paragraph that names the office, 'the clerk holding the criminal case' - identified per packet by the caption written on every pleading (District Court, East Central Judicial District, Cass County, case 09-2024-CR-001234 / -009876) - and that tells the participant to confirm local filing mechanics with it; the waiver resource is named by URL on p13. No figure is invented and the manifest's conditional-waiver rule is carried. Nuance recorded, not scored: page 32 names the clerk as the office to confirm filing mechanics with rather than saying in terms 'ask that clerk whether a filing fee applies'; a one-clause tightening would remove the ambiguity.

Repeat proof for every served party'), and that the Confidential Information Form is never served; the held official instructions p10-13 carry the State's Attorney service steps for both methods.
